title: Enteric fever (typhoid and paratyphoid)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Confirm with blood culture before antibiotics; Widal is unreliable. Fluoroquinolone resistance is widespread in India, so treat uncomplicated disease with oral azithromycin (cefixime is an alternative) and complicated disease with IV ceftriaxone, adjusting to susceptibility, for 10 to 14 days in total.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Suspect in continuous fever for several days with gastrointestinal symptoms (abdominal pain, constipation or diarrhoea), headache, coated tongue, relative bradycardia, hepatosplenomegaly.
Caused by Salmonella Typhi and Paratyphi A; paratyphoid is clinically indistinguishable and is not prevented by typhoid vaccines.

Complications usually from the second to third week: intestinal perforation (sudden abdominal pain, peritonism, shock), GI bleeding, encephalopathy (delirium, obtundation), shock, myocarditis, hepatitis, cholecystitis.
Danger features needing admission: persistent vomiting, inability to take oral medicines, severe diarrhoea, abdominal distension or tenderness, altered sensorium, hypotension, jaundice or bleeding.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Blood culture before antibiotics: a single culture is positive in about 50%; repeat cultures raise the yield. Bone marrow culture is about 80% sensitive and stays positive after antibiotics have been started.
Widal test is unreliable (cannot distinguish current, past infection or vaccination); do not diagnose or treat on Widal alone. Rapid antibody tests have limited accuracy.
CBC (leucopenia or normal count, thrombocytopenia), liver enzymes, creatinine, electrolytes; malaria smear or RDT and dengue tests in parallel.
Abdominal pain or distension: erect chest X-ray or abdominal X-ray for free gas, ultrasound or CT; surgical review.
Request susceptibility to ceftriaxone, azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, co-trimoxazole and chloramphenicol, and tailor therapy to it.

sections.title: Uncomplicated (oral)
items: Azithromycin 20 mg/kg/day orally once daily (adults 1 g/day; maximum 1 g/day). Seven-day courses are the most studied; ICMR advises 10 to 14 days of total typhoid treatment.
Alternative: cefixime 20 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses (ICMR; IAP 15 to 20 mg/kg/day) for 14 days. Clinical failure is more frequent than with azithromycin.
Co-trimoxazole (adults 1 double-strength tablet twice daily) or chloramphenicol only when the isolate is proven susceptible.
Avoid empirical fluoroquinolones: in ICMR surveillance only about 13% of S. Typhi and under 1% of S. Paratyphi A were ciprofloxacin-susceptible.
Paracetamol for fever, oral fluids and a normal diet; no food restriction is needed.
Most patients can be treated at home with close follow-up; review at 48 to 72 hours and sooner for danger features.

sections.title: Complicated or severe (IV)
items: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV once daily in adults (ICMR); children 50 to 75 mg/kg/day IV in 1 or 2 doses (IAP), not exceeding the adult daily dose. Total treatment 10 to 14 days (switch to an oral agent to complete once afebrile and eating).
No improvement after about 5 days and culture inconclusive: add azithromycin (IAP). Ceftriaxone plus azithromycin is widely used for complicated disease.
Severe typhoid with delirium, obtundation, coma or shock: dexamethasone 3 mg/kg IV over 30 minutes, then 1 mg/kg IV every 6 hours for 8 doses (WHO).
Intestinal perforation: resuscitate, nil by mouth, urgent surgery, and add anaerobic and enteric Gram-negative cover (for example metronidazole) to ceftriaxone.

Suspected XDR typhoid (for example acquired in Pakistan): azithromycin for uncomplicated disease; a carbapenem (meropenem 1 g IV 8-hourly) for complicated disease, adding a second agent if not improving (CDC).

sections.title: Monitoring and follow-up
items: Fever commonly takes up to a week to settle, and longer with cephalosporins (ICMR); do not change antibiotics for fever alone if the patient is otherwise improving. Reassess formally at day 5.
Daily abdominal examination in the second and third week for perforation or bleeding; check Hb if melaena.
Relapse occurs in up to 10% within 1 to 3 weeks of recovery; treat with a further course guided by susceptibility.
Chronic carriage develops in 1% to 4%; food handlers need stool cultures before returning to work, per local public health rules.

sections.title: Children and pregnancy
items: Children: azithromycin or cefixime orally, ceftriaxone IV. Fluoroquinolones are not approved in India under 18 years except for life-threatening infection resistant to all other options.
Pregnancy: ceftriaxone or azithromycin; avoid fluoroquinolones and chloramphenicol.
Encephalopathy or shock in a child: same dexamethasone regimen by weight, with PICU care.

sections.title: Prevention
items: Typhoid conjugate vaccine (for example Typbar-TCV, WHO-prequalified), a single dose from 6 months of age; it does not protect against Paratyphi A.
Safe drinking water, sanitation and hand hygiene.
Food safety; screen and treat chronic carriers among food handlers.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Diagnosing typhoid on a single Widal titre and missing malaria, dengue, scrub typhus or tuberculosis.
Using ciprofloxacin or ofloxacin empirically.
Starting antibiotics before drawing blood cultures.
Switching antibiotics every 2 days because fever persists, before day 5 of appropriate therapy.
Missing perforation in an obtunded patient or one on steroids, where peritonism is masked.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.dose: 20 mg/kg/day orally or IV once daily, maximum 1 g/day (adults 1 g/day)
drugs.notes: Preferred oral agent for uncomplicated disease; usually 7 days (ICMR total typhoid treatment 10 to 14 days). Check QTc with interacting drugs.

drugs.name: Cefixime
drugs.dose: 20 mg/kg/day orally in 2 divided doses for 14 days
drugs.notes: Alternative oral agent (ICMR; IAP 15 to 20 mg/kg/day). Higher failure rates.

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.dose: Adults 2 g IV once daily; children 50 to 75 mg/kg/day IV in 1 or 2 doses
drugs.notes: Complicated or severe disease; total 10 to 14 days. Do not exceed the adult daily dose in children.

drugs.name: Co-trimoxazole
drugs.dose: Adults 1 double-strength tablet (160/800 mg) orally twice daily

drugs.name: Meropenem
drugs.notes: Complicated XDR typhoid. Adjust for renal function.

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.dose: 3 mg/kg IV over 30 minutes, then 1 mg/kg IV every 6 hours for 8 doses
drugs.notes: Severe typhoid with encephalopathy or shock.
